Reindexes vectors in a database by recalculating and updating index parameters if necessary.

# Purpose
The code is a PL/pgSQL script designed to manage and potentially rebuild an index on a PostgreSQL database table named `chunkandembedding`. The script performs several operations to determine if the index needs to be rebuilt based on the number of lists, which is a parameter used in the index definition. It first retrieves the current number of lists from the existing index definition using a regular expression to parse the index definition string. If the current number of lists is not found, it defaults to zero.

The script calculates a new number of lists by taking the floor of the square root of the count of rows in the `chunkandembedding` table. It also calculates a new number of probes, which is derived as the floor of the square root of half the new lists. If the new number of lists exceeds the current number by more than 20%, the script proceeds to rebuild the index. It sets a high maintenance work memory, creates a new index with the updated number of lists, drops the old index, and renames the new index to the original name. Finally, it updates the `ivfflat.probes` setting to the new number of probes.

The script uses conditional logic to determine whether the index rebuild is necessary and provides feedback through `RAISE NOTICE` statements. This ensures that the index is only rebuilt when there is a significant change in the data distribution, optimizing the performance of the index operations.
